§290 p207b.text: Here the ugly, which does not permit of being taken away, has been concealed, there it has been re-interpreted into the sublime.

transcription.reason: The Gutenberg proofreading transcription returns HTTP 503; the Internet Archive OCR inserts the page break and printed running header within the sentence. Transcribed directly from both printed pages.
transcription.original_text: Here the ugly, which does not permit of being taken away, has been concealed, there it has been re-interpreted into the sublime.

§290 p207b.alignment: The sentence corresponds to the original here/there contrast of concealing what cannot be removed and reinterpreting it as sublime. The German past liess becomes present does not permit; flag for second reader.

§290 p207b.alignment: Read the German 1887 p. 207 and English 1910 pp. 223–224 against the printed pages; the whole sentence and punctuation match, including re-interpreted and the continuation into the sublime. Both present the ugly as concealed here and reinterpreted as sublime there. The German past liess describes what could not be removed during the shaping, while the English present does not permit states continuing resistance: a tense shift, but it retains the relevant contrast in this context.
